subject: What are best practices for Shiny apps that need to make infrequent calls external databases / API's?

messages.author: dd102d22b6d09731
messages.subject: What are best practices for Shiny apps that need to make infrequent calls external databases / API's?
parts:
Hello,

I've got a Shiny app that takes data from 2 public APIs, processes the data, and presents the results from to the user. I would like to deploy this app, but I'm concerned about too many user requests causing me to get locked out of the APIs.

I don't need to update the data more than ~ once a day, or perhaps at most a few times a day. My strategy at present is to leave the API calls outside of the shinyServer() call in server.r. My understanding, which is consistent with what happens when I run the app on locally, is that API calls are made when the app starts, but not in response to user input.

How does this work when I deploy this app to the web, as illustrated in this framework? Does the entire app, along with the API call, run only once when the application starts? Does it restart for each instance / worker / connection? Generally, what is the appropriate coding practice for what I'm trying to do?

Thanks!
